newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close higher on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close higher on foreign buying.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed higher on Thursday on foreign buying of two blue chips, but overall sentiment remained cautious ahead of March local government elections, brokers said.

The all share index closed 1.2 points up at 619.60. Price gains outnumbered losses by 22 to six. Ceylon Brewery BREW.C rose two rupees to 38.50 and National Development Bank three rupees higher at 203.
Turnover was 19.95 million rupees, led by foreign buying of blue chips Development Finance Corporation and John Keells Holdings, brokers said.

Overseas buying was worth 10.45 million and selling, 10.9 million. "Overall sentiment remains cautious as investors are waiting to see if violence before the election will pull down prices," said Sanjeeva Gunewardena, a trader at Ceylinco Stock Brokers.
A member of the opposition United National Party (UNP) was shot at by unidentified gunmen on Wednesday. A ruling coalition lawmaker was assassinated February 11.
"You can find a buyer despite the caution, if you can source a good quantity of a growth stock at a reasonable price," said Shafi Waheed, a trader at brokerage CDIC Sasoon Cumberbatch.
